note: E1 (followup_plans.md): three writer details per personal-experience dev prompt, written 2026-10-24 before any E1 generation. They answer the questions a drafter would need (a moment, a person, an outcome) and are appended to the instructions as the writer's own words.

a-narrative-drivers-test: The second time I failed, I rolled through a stop sign two blocks from the DMV.
Grandpa was waiting in his truck. He said, "The road will still be there next month."
I passed on the third try, and I drove him home that day.
a-scholarship-nursing: My mom sometimes worked double shifts and still came home and talked about her residents by name.
At the nursing home I mostly read the newspaper aloud to a man named Mr. Alvarez who had lost most of his sight.
I'm in my school's health sciences pathway and got my first aid and CPR certification this spring.
a-blog-no-social-media: The first three days I kept unlocking my phone without thinking and staring at the home screen.
I started reading at night instead and finished two novels that month.
When I came back I deleted two apps for good and kept only the group chat with my friends.
a-camp-counselor: My cousins are 6 and 9, and I'm the one who gets them through homework, dinner and bedtime on Thursdays.
At camp my favorite counselor taught me to canoe and made sure the quiet kids got picked for teams.
I want to run the arts and crafts cabin, because I already plan rainy-day projects for my cousins.
q-blog-1: I unsubscribed from every store email on the second day.
The one thing I almost bought was a pair of headphones; I waited a week and didn't want them anymore.
I saved about $150 and put it toward a summer trip.
q-blog-2: My route goes along the creek path and past the bakery that opens at 6.
I mostly listen to a history podcast and a comedy one my brother recommended.
My math teacher noticed I was answering more questions in first period.
q-personal-3: Her filling was pork, cabbage and ginger, and she folded each dumpling with exactly seven pleats.
The first three times my dough was too thick and the dumplings split when I boiled them.
Mom finally said they tasted right at our kitchen table on New Year's Eve, and we called Grandma in the hospital to tell her.
q-personal-4: I told my parents at dinner after my spring recital, where I'd made mistakes in a Chopin nocturne.
My mom didn't say much for a few days; my dad said he'd paid for eight years of lessons.
Two years later I taught myself the piano part of a song from a movie I loved, just by ear.
